artboards.title: A · Say it in a sentence — desktop
A · Say it in a sentence — mobile

annotations.text:
Four ways to make Sunk Cost feel calm. Each attacks the overwhelm along a different axis. All use the current tokens: Instrument Sans, Plex Mono, the bathymetric blues, one warm accent for the moment you surface.

The real numbers are from the live tool: Mac Studio M5 Max 64GB at $3,499 running Qwen3.8 27B, 500k tokens a day at 15:1.

A · Say it in a sentence
Axis: language over controls. The whole configuration is one editable sentence; the long model list collapses to three picks with a reason each.
Tradeoff: the tail of 16 models is behind a click, so scanning everything takes an extra step.

B · Verdict first
Axis: hierarchy. The water fills the first screen and the configuration lives inside it as pills. Everything else is one quiet reading column below, no cards.
Tradeoff: comparing models means scrolling away from the answer and back.

C · The ledger
Axis: density done calmly. One row per model, five columns, every model that fits on one screen without reading six lines per card. Verdict stays pinned on the right.
Tradeoff: least friendly for someone new to the topic; the sources and notes move behind a click.

D · Guided
Axis: progressive disclosure. Four steps, one question per screen, big targets. The answer is the last screen with a small carousel to try other models.
Tradeoff: more taps, and tweak-and-compare is slower than the live page.
